attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Matches the statement: the board fired him over candour, as it said, and not over AGI. The 'still hasn't happened' aside is kept but graded in a separate claim, which is reasonable.

contract.note: Plain reading is fair and ordinary. Tests are the board's statement, the WilmerHale summary and board members' accounts. Mapping 'not AGI' onto the review ruling out safety and pace concerns is a mild inference, but it does not decide the result.

evidence.note: AP report from Nov 17, 2023: the board fired Altman and gave lack of candour as the reason.
OpenAI's summary of the WilmerHale review says the board's statement accurately gave its rationale. This is a company disclosure summarising an outside review, so it supports 'just like they said'.
The same summary rules out safety and pace-of-development concerns and gives loss of trust as the cause. It only indirectly excludes an AGI-breakthrough motive.
Helen Toner, who voted to fire Altman, says on the record that he withheld information and lied to the board. This corroborates the candour reason.

reviews.rationale: The board said candour was the reason (e1). The WilmerHale summary says that statement was accurate, gives loss of trust as the cause, and rules out safety and pace concerns (e2, e3). A board member confirms dishonesty toward the board (e4). The packet has no evidence of an AGI motive or a pretext. The 'not AGI' part rests on indirect exclusion, but it is consistent with every item.
